Add a data file to a supplement site

Source: R/add-data.R
add_data.Rd

add_data() copies a file into the site's data/ folder and adds it as the last item of the data list in _supplement.yml. The data table on the home page of a site made from the template lists each file in that list, with its description, its size, and a download link.

Usage

add_data(file, description, path = ".")

Arguments

file

The path of the data file. Its base name must be ASCII letters, digits, ., -, and _, with no two of the symbols in a row, no . at the start, and not _ at both the start and the end. Quarto reads each value in _supplement.yml as Markdown, and these names stay as they are. The base name also cannot end in ., which Windows drops. Its part before the first . cannot be a name that Windows reserves for a device, in any letter case and with any extension: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, or LPT1 to LPT9. For example, con.csv and NUL.tar.gz are refused.

description

A short description of the file for the data table.

path

The folder of the site.

Value

The path of the file in the site's data/ folder, invisibly.

Details

If file is directly in the site's data/ folder, and not in a folder inside it, the function copies nothing and only adds it to the list, under its name on disk. Every file in data/ is published on the site, so add only data that you can share.

The function adds lines to _supplement.yml as text, so the other lines of the file, its comments included, stay as they are. It finds the data list under supplement: in block style, with each item on its own line after a -. The description is written as a YAML string in double quotes.

Errors

The function writes and copies nothing when it stops. Its own errors have the class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-empty string, file is not a single string, or description is not a single string.

  • supplement_error_no_file: file does not exist or is a folder.

  • supplement_error_line_break: description holds a line break.

  • supplement_error_file_name: the base name of file does not follow the file-name rule above. It holds a character or a run of symbols that the rule refuses, starts with ., starts and ends with _, ends in ., or its part before the first . is a name that Windows reserves for a device, in any letter case and with any extension: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, or LPT1 to LPT9.

  • supplement_error_no_metadata: path holds no _supplement.yml.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _supplement.yml, as for write_citation().

  • supplement_error_ignored_file: file is of a type that the template's .gitignore rules keep out of git: a saved R object (.rds, .rda, .RData, .qs, or .qs2), or a .rmarkdown, .quarto_ipynb, .knit.md, or .utf8.md file, in any letter case. A new site gets its .gitignore at the first render.

  • supplement_error_file_exists: data/<base name>, or a file in data/ whose name differs from it only in letter case, exists and is not file, or is a link; or data is not a folder or is a link.

  • supplement_error_already_listed: data/<base name> is already in the data list, in any letter case.

  • supplement_error_no_data_list: _supplement.yml has no data list in block style under supplement:. An empty list written as data: [] is not in block style. The error shows the lines to add by hand.

  • supplement_error_yaml: the yaml package does not read the changed _supplement.yml as the old list with the new item added. The error shows the lines to add by hand.

  • supplement_error_encoding: description or _supplement.yml is not UTF-8 text.

  • supplement_error_write: the data folder could not be made, file could not be copied, or the write of _supplement.yml failed after the file was opened, for example on a full disk. Then _supplement.yml gets its old text back.

When _supplement.yml cannot be opened for writing, for example when it is read-only, R's own error is shown. After any failed write, the function removes the copy and any folder it made.

See also

add_report() to add a report, and create_supplement() to make a site.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "data-example")
create_supplement(site)
#> ✔ Made a supplement site in /tmp/Rtmpmkqgbz/data-example.
#> ℹ Replace `OWNER/REPO` in _quarto.yml, and `OWNER` and `REPO` in the site
#>   address in _README.md, with your GitHub repository.
#> ℹ Put the paper facts in _supplement.yml.
#> ℹ Run `quarto render` in /tmp/Rtmpmkqgbz/data-example once before your first
#>   commit.
scores <- file.path(tempdir(), "scores.csv")
write.csv(data.frame(id = 1:3, score = c(4, 7, 5)), scores, row.names = FALSE)
add_data(scores, "Scores of each participant", path = site)
#> ✔ Copied /tmp/Rtmpmkqgbz/scores.csv to data/scores.csv and added it to the data
#>   list in _supplement.yml.
#> ℹ Every file in data/ is published on the site.
list.files(file.path(site, "data"))
#> [1] "example.csv" "scores.csv" 
unlink(c(site, scores), recursive = TRUE)
